title.narrative: Strengthening biodiversity, ecosystem and geodiversity conservation in UNESCO designated sites in Chile and Ecuador.

description.narrative: UNESCO designated sites in Chile and Ecuador face similar challenges in terms of governance, local community engagement and sustainable development. Ecuador has 7 Biosphere Reserves and 3 Geoparks, Chile has 10 Biosphere Reserves and 1 Geopark. Together, these sites encompass unique ecosystems (Galapagos, Amazonia, Andean Plateau, Archipelago Juan Fernandez and Patagonian Fiords) and geological formations such as basaltic columns, volcanoes, volcanic lagoons and valleys. UNESCO will focus its efforts on strengthening sites’ governance, research and local communities’ sustainable ways of living and their socioecological resilience. This will include supporting the consolidation of national governance bodies; mapping of key research being conducted in UNESCO designated sites, building local capacities to sustainable ways of living and preparedness to wildfires.
